The middle wait is 12.0 years. A pupil told police about the MP Cyril Smith in 1968 and was told Smith was "a very important, powerful man"; in 2012, two years after his death, prosecutors said he should have been charged and had been assured in 1970 that he would not be. Complaints about Jimmy Savile reached police from 1958; investigations in his lifetime brought no charges. Athletes complained about Larry Nassar from 1997. Each country is colored by the longest wait among its cases.

patterns.pattern: Deadlines, lobbying and bankruptcy
patterns.role_note: 2023: June 2023 Penal Code reform extended limitation for rape from 10 to 15 years and raised age of consent from 13 to 16; survivor group Spring said it was not enough
patterns.pattern_summary: Most survivors disclose decades later, after the legal deadline to sue or prosecute has passed. Where legislatures tried to lift those deadlines, the institutions facing claims lobbied against it, and when the deadlines fell, many filed for bankruptcy. The Catholic Church spent about $10.6 million lobbying in eight northeastern US states from 2011 to 2018; in Pennsylvania, which still has no window for old claims, the Catholic Conference spent over $7.6 million and the insurance federation nearly $20.7 million from 2014 to 2024. From 2004 to 2025, 40 US Catholic dioceses and orders filed for bankruptcy, several within hours or days of a trial, a deposition or a new law.

patterns.pattern: Waves of reckoning, and the countries that never looked
patterns.role_note: 2023: Independent probe established by Johnny & Associates, report 29 Aug 2023; UN Human Rights Council working group visit July 2023. Kitagawa repeatedly abused boys from the early 1970s to mid-2010s; 478 people claimed victimisation, 325 sought compensation (later 545 paid)
patterns.pattern_summary: Official inquiries into institutional child abuse came in waves: Canada and Ireland first (Hughes, 1989; the Ryan commission, 1999–2009), the United States in 2002–2004, most of western Europe after 2010, Australia's Royal Commission 2013–2017, then France, Portugal, Spain and Switzerland from 2021. Where inquiries used population surveys, the numbers were far above church records: about 216,000 minors abused by French clergy and religious since 1950, against about 3,000 identified before. Many "national" studies were commissioned by the church itself. Italy, Brazil, the Philippines and India, with some of the largest Catholic populations, have no national inquiry in the sources reached.

patterns.pattern: Travelling offenders: crack down here, it moves there
patterns.role: Offenders' home country: law to prosecute abroad
patterns.role_note: 1999: Japan: 1999 Law for Punishing Acts Related to Child Prostitution and Child Pornography applies to Japanese nationals abroad
patterns.pattern_summary: Child sex tourism followed enforcement around the map. Observers reported that child prostitution in Svay Pak, Cambodia, grew after Thailand cracked down in the 1990s, and that when police raided Svay Pak in January 2003 the raid had been announced in advance and most of the children had been moved to Siem Reap and Sihanoukville. When Manila closed Ermita in 1992, businesses moved to Angeles City. Offenders' home countries passed laws to prosecute their citizens for abuse abroad (Germany 1993, Australia 1994, Canada 1997, Japan 1999, the US PROTECT Act 2003). Then the trade moved online: in the Philippines, street and establishment child sex trafficking fell 79–86% in targeted cities (2006–2016), while monthly Philippine internet addresses used for child sexual exploitation rose more than twelvefold (2014–2017).

cases.title: Johnny Kitagawa — Johnny & Associates talent agency
cases.who: Johnny Kitagawa (founder, Johnny & Associates; now Smile-Up)
cases.what: An external investigation set up by Johnny & Associates concluded on 29 Aug 2023 that founder Johnny Kitagawa had sexually abused minors aspiring to be pop singers for decades; the BBC summarises the finding as abuse of hundreds of boys and young men over a six-decade career. The company admitted the abuse in September 2023, split into a new talent agency (Starto Entertainment) and Smile-Up, which handles compensation through a relief committee of three former judges. The BBC documentary 'Predator' (March 2023) and a former trainee's public allegations in April 2023 triggered the reckoning. In March 2024 Smile-Up's CEO told the BBC he believed two more perpetrators had worked at the agency. Kitagawa died in 2019 and was never charged.
cases.cover_up: Media silence: Shukan Bunshun's 2001 reports were upheld on the sexual allegations by the courts (damages reduced 2003; Supreme Court rejected appeal 2004), yet Japanese media barely covered them; journalists attributed this to the agency's power over talent bookings. Earliest cited report: Weekly Sankei, 1965.

cases.title: Okinawa — rape of a 12-year-old girl by three US servicemen (1995)
cases.who: US Navy and Marine Corps personnel from Camp Hansen
cases.what: In September 1995 three US servicemen based on Okinawa abducted and raped a 12-year-old Okinawan schoolgirl. They were tried in a Japanese court and in 1996 were each found guilty and sentenced to between six years and six months and seven years in prison. The case triggered mass protests against the US bases.

patterns.pattern: False alarms that drown real cases
patterns.role_note: Kenya — RTÉ 'Mission to Prey' and false allegation against Fr Kevin Reynolds.
patterns.pattern_summary: Invented trafficking stories take resources from real ones. In July 2020 the US National Human Trafficking Hotline received hundreds of reports about a false claim that the furniture seller Wayfair was selling children; the hotline's operator, Polaris, said the volume made it harder to help people who needed it, and none of the reports had new information. "Pizzagate" led to a man firing a rifle inside a Washington restaurant in 2016. London's Metropolitan Police spent over £2 million on Operation Midland, built on a "VIP ring" story invented by Carl Beech, who was himself jailed for child-abuse offences. The McMartin preschool trials in the 1980s cost about $15 million and ended without a conviction.

cases.title: Kenya — babies stolen and sold in Nairobi, incl. from a government hospital (BBC Africa Eye)
cases.who: Street child-snatchers working for a buyer; illegal street clinics; a clinical social worker at a government hospital
cases.what: A year-long BBC Africa Eye investigation (November 2020) found children snatched from homeless mothers in Nairobi and sold for about £350–550, illegal street clinics selling newborns (one offered an unborn child for about £315 while paying the mother £70), and a clinical social worker at the government-run Mama Lucy Kibaki Hospital who sold an abandoned two-week-old boy to undercover reporters for 300,000 shillings (£2,000) using legitimate transfer paperwork. The reporters delivered all the children to a children's home. The BBC said the official appeared to keep his job and the clinic appeared to still operate.

cases.title: Kenya — child sex trafficking in Kilifi/Kwale villas; Karamoja girls to Nairobi (US TIP 2025)
cases.who: Family members, taxi drivers, recruiters; foreign and local offenders
cases.what: The 2025 US TIP report cites a 2023 NGO study estimating that more than 2,000 children were exploited in child sex trafficking in Kilifi and Kwale counties, increasingly in private villas and vacation homes rather than hotels. It also reports cross-border rings moving women and underage girls from Uganda's Karamoja region to Nairobi, and truck drivers, miners and Lake Victoria fishermen exploiting children.
cases.cover_up: The report notes ongoing concerns of official complicity with no reported action against complicit officials.

cases.title: Kenya — RTÉ 'Mission to Prey' and false allegation against Fr Kevin Reynolds
cases.who: Irish missionaries in Kenya; RTÉ
cases.what: RTÉ's May 2011 Prime Time Investigates documentary 'Mission to Prey' reported on clerical abuse by missionaries in Africa. It wrongly accused Irish priest Fr Kevin Reynolds of fathering a child with a minor in Kenya; the allegation was shown to be untrue, RTÉ apologised and paid him a substantial libel settlement, its director general called it 'one of the gravest mistakes' RTÉ had made, and the Taoiseach cited a 'grievous' drop in standards. The Broadcasting Authority of Ireland opened an investigation. Separately in 2011 a Dutch bishop was investigated over alleged abuse of a minor 18 years earlier when he was a priest in Ngong diocese, and was retired by the church.

patterns.pattern_summary: When a priest, brother, teacher or headmistress was found abusing children, the institution often moved them rather than calling the police: to another parish, another school, another state, or another continent. patterns.pattern_summary: The map's documented record is thickest where people looked. Childlight's 2026 update rests on representative surveys from only 60 countries; South Asia, West and Central Africa and the Middle East and North Africa lack them. The UN's 2024 global trafficking report covered 156 countries, but only 72 supplied 2023 data. In 2025, 14% of the 23.4 million reports to the US CyberTipline could not be placed in any country, and North Korea had 12. Countries with large churches and many children's institutions, such as Italy, Brazil, the Philippines and India, have held no national inquiry into institutional abuse in the sources reached. Where a country is colored only by estimate on this map, this is why.
